eyeItems.title: The creative-register court — eight arms of your cyborg brief (C′ rerun valid as of 26 Aug 02:35)
eyeItems.question: Does the creative register (arm C) reach your raw prompt’s conviction (arm A, and your two reference frames) while keeping sheet structure? Check each frame against your own list: jaw plate present and prominent, amber eye glowing, porcelain committed, no beards you never asked for, build spread not converged, wardrobe line obeyed. Refusal counts are under each strip’s caption.

frames.caption: Your reference frame 1 — the conviction bar, made by your own raw prompt.
Your reference frame 2 — the second raw-prompt frame.
Your raw prompt + your seven words of frame, re-made tonight. 0 of 3 refused. This is the bar the candidate must reach.
Today’s full compile, through the real entrance. 0 of 3 refused — but look: beards you never asked for on all three, t-shirts against the bare-chested ask, and the hardware gone timid.

THE CANDIDATE — the creative register: your words verbatim, a minimal frame, a per-slice variance card. 1 of 3 refused. Hardware committed — but the mid-torso framing line was ignored (full body delivered), so the lean frame loses locks the old scaffolding held.
The candidate minus the variance card. 2 OF 3 REFUSED — the card appears to protect against refusals as well as buying spread.
The candidate plus the one-sentence category block. 2 of 3 refused.

RERUN, now valid: the same three compiles as B with every house block cut to its first clause and YOUR facts kept word for word (12,500 → 3,300 characters). 0 of 3 refused. Against B: the beards, the shirts and the missing porcelain are still here — shortening did not fix them, so those answers are WRONG, not long. What it bought is conviction: a solid jaw plate in frames 1 and 3, and a tighter mid-torso frame.
The writer’s room: “cyber-goth girl with an eyepatch”, authored into rich concepts, rendered. 1 of 3 refused; the author gave 4 concepts of the 8 asked.
The same thin brief through today’s compile — the control for the writer’s room.

journal.text: Quiet night, on purpose. No reply from you yet on the court strips, so nothing moved on the creative register — the next step (building the register dark) starts only on your word. The one thing that could be done without you was done: a maintenance fix (#71) so that a fresh copy of the code on a Windows machine no longer trips seven of our own test suites over invisible line-ending differences. It went through the gate green and is in this deploy; it changes nothing you or a customer would see, it just stops the team losing time to a phantom failure on every new working copy. The OpenRouter balance card above still stands — $7.52 left on the text engine every roll and refine needs; please check auto-top-up when you're up. Waiting for you: your verdict on the eight strips in the gallery (reply under the item).

The court's one invalid arm is rerun and valid. Last night's C′ strip measured a harness mistake — its shortening had cut your character detail down to the word 'Bald'. Overnight it was rebuilt so your own words are kept letter for letter and only the house's photography instructions are shortened, checked against the exact same three compiles as arm B before a cent was spent, then rendered: 3 frames, none refused, about 17 cents. What it shows, for your eye: the beards you never asked for, the shirts over a bare-chested ask and the missing porcelain skin are ALL still there in the short version — so those are wrong answers, not long ones. What the shortening did buy is commitment: the jaw plate reads as a real plate and the frame comes in to mid-torso. All eight strips now sit in the gallery for your verdict; nothing else moves on the register until you've looked. Also: your OpenRouter account (the text engine every roll needs) is down to $7.52 — see the problem card above; no request was queued today, only his word to note it.

THE COURT RAN. Eight arms of your cyborg brief, 18 renders, $0.79 — the strips are in your gallery above, in the full-size viewer you asked for this evening. What’s already visible before your eye: today’s compile put beards you never asked for on all three frames and dressed your bare-chested ask in t-shirts; the lean register carries committed hardware but broke the mid-torso framing lock; and the LEANER the prompt, the MORE the engine refused (the no-variance-card arm refused 2 of 3), so the design’s safety-rewording retry is load-bearing. One arm (C′) is reported invalid — the harness’s own shortening cut your character detail, so its frames measure my mistake, honestly labelled. Your verdict goes in the box under the item; full pointers on #16.

Fixed your admin-entry complaint (#68): typing /admin was a dead end (a 404) — it now lands on the overview — and the account menu's own text was invisible in dark theme; both driven and photographed before and after. The same drive found the lobby's theme toggle is unclickable (filed as #73). Caught and repaired a record gap your go-live exposed: the test that guards the migration ledger wasn't updated when the ceremony ran, so every change's checks were failing; fix is in review (PR 76). Then rebuilt this page toward your UX feedback (#74): the chips at the top, the milestone progress bar, all eight ladder rungs, Recently landed, and the journal fold you are using now.

Built this page and proved it in the running app: a reply typed here landed in the database and came back through the crew's own read script, and with the flag off the tab vanishes entirely. Your two Desk taps are on the record — the ladder is signed (N1–N8 governs) and the face-scan pair is widened to everyone in the beta. Both cards below are marked done.

Closed the urgent refine double-charge question: the guard was built a week before it was filed as missing — a second tap on a paid edit has been refused free since 08-18. Merged the record fix and pinned the wire in the test suite (#54, PR 67). Designed and started building this page (#41).

FOUNDER RULING — THE SPEND THRESHOLD, verbatim: “i thought we established it doesnt need my permission to do this unless it plans to spend a massive amount of money like $50+”. In the Program: under-$50 courts/measurements run without asking (estimate and actual recorded on the issue); $50+ comes to him priced. The creative-register court is therefore FUNDED. Also filed on his eye: #74, Crew tab UX parity with the Desk (progress bars, full ladder, chips, Done section) — urgent-labelled.

THIS PAGE IS NOW THE DESK. Your word before bed, verbatim: “ensure that the live crew tab is the new desk and everything is pointed towards it to be updated rather than the old desk … the forman is all sweet to continue working as long as the desk is being updated so when i wake up in the morning i have somthing to look at.” Done: the shift orders now read your replies from this page and write this briefing every shift, shipped with each deploy; the old Desk page is retired as a read-only mirror. Landed in this deploy: your lobby→admin fix (#68), this page’s progress bars, full ladder, chips and Recently landed (#74), and the eye gallery (#75) — empty until the register court’s frames arrive. Filed for the shift, urgent: #82 (three hardening findings on the gallery’s image route from its review, due before the first frames) and the full-size image viewer you asked for (on #75). Tonight’s gate stall was a merge conflict on the auto-generated architecture map, not GitHub — the class is filed as #80.
